title: Secret grep in security-cra is case-sensitive and misses apiKey and API_KEY
body:
## Summary
Make the H3 secret grep (security-cra gather step 5) case-insensitive and let the key name carry a prefix or suffix, so the rank-1 finding of the pack (a live secret, impact 10) is found in camelCase and UPPER_SNAKE code.

## Description
skill/lenses/security-cra.md:72 runs `git grep -n -I -E "(api[_-]?key|secret|token|passw(or)?d)\s*[:=]..."` with no `-i`. The name alternatives are lower case, so `const apiKey = 'sk_live_...'` (capital K), `API_KEY="..."`, `authToken: '...'` and `PASSWORD = '...'` never match. Even with `-i`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY = '...'` misses because `secret` must be followed directly by `[:=]`. The fixture that measures the lens seeds only the lowercase snake form (skill/scripts/tests/fixtures/lens-fixture/src/config.js:13), so lens-eval cannot see the gap: the fixture was shaped to the pattern, not to how secrets are written.

## Flow
- agent runs security-cra gather step 5 as written
- repo holds `const apiKey = 'sk_live_...'` in a shipped config
- grep exits 1; H3 is reported checked with 0 hits
- the live key never becomes a card

## Expected impact
The rank-1 security finding is found whatever the naming convention. Risk: more E0 hits to clear (tests, examples), which step 5 already handles.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - H3 finds live secrets under the naming conventions real code uses
Before: probe: 0 of 5 camel/upper lines matched (apiKey, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, API_KEY, stripeSecret, PASSWORD)
After: 4 of 5 with `-i` alone (probe); 5 of 5 once the name may carry `[A-Za-z_]*` around it (simulation on STRIPE_SECRET_KEY)
Method: probe - ran the pattern verbatim with git grep in a scratch repo outside the tree, with and without -i
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/lenses/security-cra.md:72: 5. **Secrets.** `git grep -n -I -E "(api[_-]?key|secret|token|passw(or)?d)\s*[:=]\s*['\"][A-Za-z0-9/+_\-]{12,}['\"]|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"`. | probe as written: exit 1, 0 matches; with -i: s.js:1 apiKey, s.js:3 API_KEY, s.js:4 stripeSecret, s.js:5 PASSWORD (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY still missed) | skill/scripts/tests/fixtures/lens-fixture/src/config.js:13: api_key: 'psk_live_4fQ9xT2mB7vK1nR8cL3wZ6',
impact_why: The pack rank-1 hypothesis (live secret, impact 10) silently misses the two most common naming styles

title: Template-literal SQL alternative in the risky-pattern grep can never match
body:
## Summary
Fix the `\$\{` alternative of security-cra gather step 6 so interpolated SQL (`SELECT ... ${id}`) is listed. Inside a double-quoted bash string it reaches git grep as `$\{`: an end-of-line anchor followed by `{`, which matches nothing.

## Description
skill/lenses/security-cra.md:77 writes `(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE) .*(['\"] *\+|\$\{)` inside a double-quoted argument. In bash (the Claude Code Bash tool, codex exec) `\$` inside double quotes becomes `$`, and `$` is an anchor in ERE, so only concatenation is found. Both SQL findings the fixture expects use `+` (skill/scripts/tests/fixtures/lens-fixture/src/routes/search.js:12, src/jobs/nightly-report.js:27), so lens-eval cannot catch it. Under PowerShell the string passes through literally, so the miss depends on the shell. Fix: put the pattern in single quotes, or write the dollar as `[$]`.

## Flow
- agent copies step 6 into bash
- the shell turns `\$\{` into `$\{`
- a route building `SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = ${req.query.id}` is not listed
- H2 at E3 (impact 8) goes unreported

## Expected impact
H2 is found for template-literal SQL, the dominant style in modern JS/TS. Risk: none beyond a pack wording patch.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - H2 sinks built by interpolation are listed
Before: probe: pattern as written matched the concatenation line and not the `${id}` line (1 of 2)
After: probe: the single-quoted `'...\$\{'` form matched the `${id}` line (2 of 2 with the concatenation alternative)
Method: probe - ran both forms with git grep in a scratch repo under bash
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/lenses/security-cra.md:77: ...|v-html|(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE) .*(['\"] *\+|\$\{)|pickle\.loads|... | probe as written: only `a.js:2:const r = "SELECT * FROM t WHERE a = " + a;` | single-quoted: `a.js:1:const q = `SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ${id}`;`
impact_why: An E3 injection sink class (impact 8 in the pack) is invisible whenever SQL is interpolated rather than concatenated

title: A stale machine pre-triage mark skips the person on a demoted slice
body:
## Summary
A card's `pretriaged_by = machine:dowser` is never cleared, so when the card resurfaces in a later run `pretriageRun` reports it pre-triaged again without checking the slice's current level - even after the slice was demoted to L0.

## Description
- skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:198 `if (r.pretriaged_by === MACHINE_DECIDER) { pretriaged.push(item); continue; }` runs before the level check at skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:199.
- The mark is written once at skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:189 (`... AND pretriaged_by IS NULL`) and no code path resets it: the only writers of the column in skill/ are skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:189 and skill/scripts/lib/hydrate.mjs:23 (copy from Forge).
- skill/scripts/lib/triage.mjs:34 `const person = all.filter((r) => r.pretriaged_by !== MACHINE)` then removes the card from the person's pre-triage list, and the push carries the mark into the inbox.
- The contract (docs/contracts/scan-finding-1.md:60) puts the gate in the store: it 'refuses a machine decision above' the slice's level.

## Flow
- Run 1: slice technical|doc-drift|-|S at L1; card A predicted accept is marked machine:dowser.
- A person rejects another machine-marked card B -> reversal -> slice drops to L0.
- A person snoozes A; A resurfaces in run 2 with new evidence (snoozed -> candidate -> verified).
- pretriage --run run2: A is listed under `pretriaged` with `level: 0`; the person never pre-triages it.

## Expected impact
The demotion that exists to put the person back in the loop is bypassed for exactly the cards that were machine-handled before. Fix: clear `pretriaged_by` when a card leaves `verified/pushed` for `candidate` (resurface) or re-evaluate the level at line 198 for any card whose last_run_id is this run.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the L1 gate holds on a demoted slice.
Before: probe returns pretriaged [{fp: 152582c2054ffec4, slice: technical|doc-drift|-|S, level: 0}], for_person [].
After: the same card lands in for_person at level 0 (a re-check of the level, or a cleared mark on resurface).
Method: probe - a scratch script outside the repo drove the real store (propose, move, allocateRun, pretriageRun) through the flow above; the fix itself was not built (ideas-only).
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: Probe output: `level now 0` then `run2 pretriage {"pretriaged":[{"fp":"152582c2054ffec4","slice":"technical|doc-drift|-|S","level":0}],"for_person":[]}`; skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:198 `if (r.pretriaged_by === MACHINE_DECIDER) { pretriaged.push(item); continue; }`; skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:189 `UPDATE proposals SET pretriaged_by = ? WHERE fp = ? AND status = 'verified' AND pretriaged_by IS NULL`; grep for a statement setting pretriaged_by to NULL over skill/ and forge/src: 0 hits.
impact_why: The trust gate's demotion is bypassed for resurfaced cards: a level-0 slice still skips the person's pre-triage.

title: No test diffs manifest.yml against the code's key lists
body:
## Summary
Four hand-kept lists must agree with forge/manifest.yml: TOOL_NAMES, ROVO_ACTIONS, MODULE_KEYS and the index.js KEYS. No test reads the manifest, so a mismatch reaches production unseen.

## Description
forge/manifest.yml:21-36 (rovo:mcp tools), :38-169 (action keys, each with a function), :195-231 (resource modules) are the platform ground truth. The code mirrors them in forge/src/core/app.mjs:52-56 (TOOL_NAMES, ROVO_ACTIONS), forge/src/core/app.mjs:304-309 (MODULE_KEYS) and forge/src/index.js:90-92 (KEYS). `grep -n "manifest" forge/test/*.mjs` finds no test that loads it. The known missing byline.draftFix in forge/src/index.js:90 (already filed) is exactly the drift such a test catches. Today the other lists agree: 12 tools = 12 TOOL_NAMES, 4 resource modules = 4 MODULE_KEYS.

## Flow
- a tool is added to TOOL_NAMES and its handler, but not to rovo:mcp tools in the manifest
- all 155 tests pass
- forge deploy ships a tool no agent can call; or the reverse, a manifest action with no handler answers bad-input

## Expected impact
Add one test that parses manifest.yml (a small line parser is enough, no new dependency), then asserts: the set of rovo:mcp tools equals TOOL_NAMES; the action keys equal TOOL_NAMES plus ROVO_ACTIONS; each action's function is mcp or rovo, matching its list; the resource-module keys equal Object.keys(MODULE_KEYS); and the index.js KEYS (read as source, as adapter-identity.test.mjs does) equal Object.keys(RESOLVERS).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - manifest/code drift fails a test.
Before: no test reads the manifest; the known KEYS gap passed 155/155.
After: the known gap and any future tool/module drift fail.
Method: simulation - checked the three lists by hand today (consistent except the known KEYS gap); walked added-tool, removed-action and new-resolver-key cases.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: `grep -rn "manifest.yml" forge/test/*.mjs` -> no matches; forge/manifest.yml:22-36 `- key: dowser-mcp ... tools: - dowser_sources_tickets ... - dowser_work_report`; forge/src/core/app.mjs:52 `export const TOOL_NAMES = /** @type {const} */ (['dowser_sources_tickets', ...`; npm --prefix forge test: tests 155, pass 155
impact_why: Platform wiring is the one contract unit tests cannot see; a mismatch already shipped once

title: Evidence added to a verified or pushed card reaches Jira without verify
body:
## Summary
A re-propose that adds new evidence to a `verified` or `pushed` card appends the evidence but leaves the status alone, so `verify` never checks the new quotes, yet `outbox` sends them.

## Description
`propose` handles an existing fp outside snoozed/rejected/dropped by appending evidence and returning `evidence-grew` with the status unchanged (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:254, skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:270). `verify` only walks `candidate` cards (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:374, skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:201). `outbox` selects every `verified` card and every `pushed` card whose evidence seq grew since the last push (skill/scripts/lib/sync.mjs:141-147) and sends all stored evidence. So a quote that is not in the file is shown in the Jira inbox as if verified. D8 (detection and verification are separate, docs/data-model.md:269) does not hold for these cards.

## Flow
- run 1: propose card with a real quote, verify -> verified
- run 2: same fp, plus a fabricated quote -> `evidence-grew`, status verified
- verify run 2 checks 0 cards
- outbox sends both quotes

## Expected impact
Every card the inbox shows carries only quotes that verify found at the run's head. Fix options: move a verified/pushed card with a new code/doc key back through a check (verify the new keys only, in `verify --run`, by selecting cards whose asserted keys are newer than their last verify transition), or hold the new keys out of the outbox until checked.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no unverified quote reaches the inbox
Before: probe sent ['# Dowser data model', 'THIS LINE DOES NOT EXIST ANYWHERE'] for a verified card; verify checked 0 cards
After: the fabricated quote would be dropped or held back (simulation of the fix: verify selecting grown verified/pushed cards would run findQuote and fail it with quote-not-found)
Method: probe - a scratch script outside the repo drove openStore(':memory:'), propose, verifyRun, outbox against the real lib; the fix itself was not built (ideas-only)
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:269-270 `if (status === 'candidate') refreshCard();\n    return ... clean({ result: added > 0 ? 'evidence-grew' : 'duplicate', fp, added, status, note })`; skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:374 `SELECT fp FROM proposals WHERE last_run_id = ? AND status = 'candidate'`; skill/scripts/lib/sync.mjs:141 `SELECT fp, status FROM proposals WHERE status IN ('verified', 'pushed')`. Probe output: `{ result: 'evidence-grew', status: 'verified' }`, `verify2 checked 0`, outbox `[ 'verified', [ '# Dowser data model', 'THIS LINE DOES NOT EXIST ANYWHERE' ] ]`
impact_why: Unchecked quotes in the inbox break the core promise that every card's evidence was mechanically verified

title: Dev-only check reads the root lockfile while deps audits nested ones
body:
## Summary
Make security-cra gather step 3 run its scope checks against the lockfile the `dep` ref names (`<lockfile path>#pkg@ver`), not a hardcoded root `package-lock.json`.

## Description
Step 2 (skill/lenses/security-cra.md:54-57) says `deps` audits manifest directories up to three levels down and every ref is `<lockfile path>#<package>@<version>`. Step 3 (line 63) checks dev-only with `git grep -n -A6 '"node_modules/<pkg>"' -- package-lock.json`, a pathspec that matches only the root file, and finds the parent the same way (line 65). In this repo the root grep for vite returns nothing, while forge/static/app/package-lock.json:2673-2677 holds `"node_modules/vite"` with `"dev": true`. A nested dev-only advisory then reads as shipped; the pack forbids E0 cards (line 113) but this step cannot tell.

## Flow
- deps returns a ref `forge/static/app/package-lock.json#vite@<v>` at high
- step 3 greps the root package-lock.json: no entry, no `"dev": true`
- agent classes it shipped with no import path (rank 4, impact 5)
- a dev-only advisory becomes a card the person rejects as false-positive

## Expected impact
Fewer false-positive H1 cards on monorepos and Forge/Custom UI layouts; each such rejection also costs the technical slice trust. Risk: none, wording.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - H1 scope is judged from the lockfile that carries the advisory
Before: probe: the root-only grep finds 0 entries for a package that is dev-only in a nested lockfile
After: probe: with the ref path as pathspec the `"dev": true` line shows
Method: probe - ran both greps in this repo
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/lenses/security-cra.md:56: the root (an `auditors` entry below the root carries `dir`). Each `ref` is `<lockfile path>#<package>@<version>`; its `title` is | skill/lenses/security-cra.md:63: `"node_modules/<pkg>"` carries `"dev": true` (`git grep -n -A6 '"node_modules/<pkg>"' -- package-lock.json`), | probe: root grep empty; `-- '**/package-lock.json'` -> forge/static/app/package-lock.json:2673 "node_modules/vite": {, forge/static/app/package-lock.json-2677 "dev": true,
impact_why: Every nested-lockfile advisory is mis-scoped; dev-only ones become false-positive cards

title: Isolate test git from the developer's config: commit.gpgsign fails the suite
body:
## Summary
The fixtures run git commit under the user's global and system config; with commit signing on, every test that builds a repo fails.

## Description
skill/scripts/tests/_fixture.mjs:65-74 (gitRepo) sets only user.email, user.name and core.autocrlf, then `git commit -q -m init` with the inherited environment. Direct commits do the same in skill/scripts/tests/areas.test.mjs:45, core-hardening.test.mjs:228-234, delivery.test.mjs:40, paths.test.mjs:59-61. A global commit.gpgsign=true, a core.hooksPath with a commit-msg hook, init.templateDir hooks or a system config therefore change or break the suite. No test sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM (git grep: zero hits); only tools/lens-eval.mjs:159 passes --no-verify.

## Flow
- A contributor signs commits globally (common for verified GitHub commits)
- `npm test` -> every gitRepo-based test fails in before()
- They cannot run the documented gate without editing their own git config

## Expected impact
Set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL to an empty temp file and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 for test git (e.g. in _fixture.mjs, exported as a gitEnv used by every direct git call), or pass -c commit.gpgsign=false -c core.hooksPath= on commits.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the suite is independent of the machine's git config
Before: probe: `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2 commit.gpgsign=true gpg.program=false node --test skill/scripts/tests/paths.test.mjs` -> tests 4, pass 0, fail 4; without the env -> pass 4
After: the same env leaves paths.test.mjs at pass 4
Method: probe - injected the config through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT for one test file; the after side needs the fixture change
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/tests/_fixture.mjs:73 `git('commit', '-q', '-m', 'init');` (no -c overrides, inherited env); probe output `ℹ tests 4 / ℹ pass 0 / ℹ fail 4` with commit.gpgsign=true vs `ℹ pass 4 / ℹ fail 0` without; `git grep GIT_CONFIG skill/scripts/tests` -> no hits
impact_why: Anyone with signed commits or global hooks cannot run the gate; a test env leak is also a source of flakes.

title: move lets an agent or the store reject or snooze a card; only accept is guarded
body:
## Summary
Guard `verified|pushed -> rejected|snoozed` (and merge into a card the agent did not find as a same-work duplicate) to `human:` and `forge:` deciders in DECIDER_GUARDS, as SKILL.md and triage.md state, so a rejection can never come from the agent.

## Description
SKILL.md:544 says "Only a human accepts, rejects, snoozes or merges into another person's item", and skill/references/triage.md:14-15 list `verified -> rejected` and `verified -> snoozed` as "human". The code guards only acceptance: skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:101-103 `DECIDER_GUARDS = { 'verified>accepted': ['human'] }`, checked at skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:348. `triage apply` requires `human:` (skill/scripts/lib/triage.mjs:133) and so do rules (memory.mjs:437), but a single `move` does not. A probe recorded `move --to rejected --by agent:claude` and `--to snoozed --by skill:dowser` on verified cards. A rejected card is in `suppressed` for its lens from then on (memory.mjs:174-176), so an agent that "tidies" a card buries it for every later scan, and trust.mjs:49 does not count it, so nobody sees the prediction it overrode.

## Flow
- agent, mid-triage, runs `move <fp> --to rejected --by agent:claude-code --reason not-worth-it`
- move checks canMove and deciderAllowed: verified>rejected is unguarded
- card becomes rejected, decided_by agent:claude-code
- every later context lists it in suppressed; outbox never pushes it; the person never saw it

## Expected impact
The "a person decides every proposal" promise holds in code, not only in the procedure. Risk: low; a forge: verdict and human: moves keep working; a test that moves with agent: or skill: for these targets must change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the store refuses decisions the procedure reserves for people
Before: probe: 2 of 2 non-human decisions recorded (rejected by agent:claude, snoozed by skill:dowser)
After: simulation: both refused with exit 2 "needs a human decider"; human:runner reject, forge:<user> verdict, and skill:dowser wake (snoozed -> verified) still pass
Method: probe - scratch script outside the repo against a temp store with the lib move()
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:102: 'verified>accepted': Object.freeze(['human']), | skill/SKILL.md:544: - **Never self-approve.** Only a human accepts, rejects, snoozes or merges into another person's | skill/references/triage.md:14: | `verified` | `rejected` | human | `move --to rejected --reason <code>` (pre-triage) | | probe output: "rejected agent:claude -> rejected agent:claude", "snoozed skill:dowser -> snoozed skill:dowser"
impact_why: An agent decision silently suppresses a verified card forever and bypasses the trust ledger, against the stated invariant

title: Page banner asks Jira permissions per inbox on every Confluence page view
body:
## Summary
byline.forPage resolves the caller's visible inboxes (one /mypermissions call per distinct Jira project) before it looks up whether the page has any Dowser link, and the page banner calls it on every page view in the site.

## Description
app.mjs:260 evaluates `await acc.visibleKeys()` as an argument, so access.mjs:87-90 reads every inbox and calls canSee for each before cards.mjs:330 bylineForPage runs its indexed page_links read. The banner module (manifest confluence:pageBanner dowser-doc-banner) renders on every page and calls byline.forPage on mount (static/app/src/routes/byline/Banner.jsx:15). The doc-drift.mjs header says an unlinked page should cost "one indexed lookup".

## Flow
- person opens any Confluence page
- banner calls byline.forPage
- listInboxRows + N Jira permission requests
- page_links answers zero rows; banner renders nothing

## Expected impact
An unlinked page view costs one indexed read and no Jira calls; fewer GB-seconds and no Jira rate-limit pressure from browsing Confluence.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - Jira requests per unlinked page view
Before: 20 permission calls and 3 statements on a site with 20 inboxes, measured
After: 1 statement and 0 permission calls: read page_links first and return early when empty, then check access only for the inboxes the links name
Method: probe - scratch script: 20 inboxes each bound to its own Jira project, runResolver byline.forPage on an unlinked page with the fake Perms port counting calls
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: "byline unlinked page: statements 3 perm calls 20 0"; forge/src/core/app.mjs:260 `'byline.forPage': async (d, p, _, __, acc) => bylineForPage(d.db, needStr(p, 'page_id'), await acc.visibleKeys()),`; forge/src/core/access.mjs:89 `const ok = await Promise.all(rows.map((r) => canSee(r)));`
impact_why: every Confluence page view on the site pays N Jira calls for a banner that is almost always empty

title: A hydrated card that wakes from snooze can never be pushed
body:
## Summary
`hydrate` writes `provenance.hydrated_from` into the stored provenance. That key is not part of the record: the model's validator and the schema both refuse unknown provenance keys. When a hydrated snoozed card wakes (`snoozed -> verified`), `outbox` sends it with that key and Forge's `checkRecord` refuses it, every push, forever.

## Description
skill/scripts/lib/hydrate.mjs:94 stores `{ ...it.provenance, hydrated_from: 'dowser_memory_pull' }`. validateCandidate refuses unknown provenance keys (skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:473-474); the schema's provenance is `additionalProperties: false` (skill/schema/dowser-proposal-2.schema.json, $defs.provenance). Forge runs `validateCandidate(cand, { wire: true })` on each pushed record (forge/src/core/push.mjs:119). `wakeSnoozed` moves the card to verified without refreshing provenance (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:42-50); only a resurface to candidate re-writes it (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:266).

## Flow
- teammate hydrates; an item snoozed in Jira with a past date comes in
- next run start wakes it -> verified
- outbox includes it with provenance.hydrated_from
- Forge: invalid record: provenance:unknown field hydrated_from; it stays verified and is re-sent each outbox

## Expected impact
Hydrated cards push like any other: keep the marker outside the record (e.g. the hydrate run id is already `first_run_id`, harness `dowser-hydrate`), or strip it in `proposalRecord`.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a woken hydrated card is accepted by the push validator
Before: probe -> `forge wire validation: { ok: false, why: 'provenance:unknown field hydrated_from' }`
After: without the key the same record validates (simulation: the remaining provenance {lens_version:'1'} passes model.mjs:471-481)
Method: probe - scratch script ran hydrate, runStart (woke the card), outbox and validateCandidate wire on the real libs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/hydrate.mjs:94 `provenance_json: JSON.stringify({ ...it.provenance, hydrated_from: 'dowser_memory_pull' }),`; skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:473-474 `const pvx = extraKey(pv, ['lens_version', 'model', 'harness', 'run_id', 'focus']);\n  if (pvx) return no(\`provenance:unknown field ${pvx}\`);`; forge/src/core/push.mjs:119 `const v = validateCandidate(cand, { wire: true });`; probe: `woke [ '2fbea79e5b6e8dc7' ]`, `provenance { lens_version: '1', hydrated_from: 'dowser_memory_pull' }`, `forge wire validation: { ok: false, why: 'provenance:unknown field hydrated_from' }`
impact_why: Every hydrated snooze that wakes is stuck: refused by Forge on each push, never back in the inbox

title: Latest outcome is picked by insert id; Forge's first page arrives newest-first
body:
## Summary
reflect.mjs takes an item's 'latest' outcome as MAX(id), i.e. the last row inserted. Forge's first reflect sync (no `outcomes_since`) returns outcomes newest first, so the skill inserts them in descending time and MAX(id) is the OLDEST rating. The judge's memory then quotes a superseded rating, and `context` disagrees with the quality ledger, which orders by recorded_at.

## Description
- skill/scripts/lib/reflect.mjs:184 `o.id = (SELECT MAX(o2.id) FROM outcomes o2 WHERE o2.fp = o.fp)` (outcomeCounts) and skill/scripts/lib/reflect.mjs:206 (outcomeNotes, the memory the judge reads before predicting).
- skill/scripts/lib/reflect.mjs:159-161 inserts outcomes in response order.
- forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:101 `ORDER BY recorded_at DESC, ref DESC LIMIT ${OUTCOMES_MAX}` when outcomes_since is absent; docs/contracts/forge-mcp-2.md:396 'without outcomes_since, the newest 200 outcomes of the project, newest first'.
- skill/scripts/lib/quality.mjs:86 picks the latest by `ORDER BY o.recorded_at DESC, o.id DESC` - the two rules disagree.
- skill/scripts/lib/reflect.mjs:221 outcomesOf orders by id and is documented 'oldest first' - also reversed for first-page rows.
- The mock hides it: tools/mock-forge-mcp.mjs:492 returns `p.outcomes.slice(-OUTCOMES_MAX)` oldest first, unlike Forge.

## Flow
- A person rates DW-1 `wrong` (Nov 1), then `right` after a fix (Nov 2).
- First `reflect sync` on this store: Forge sends [right Nov 2, wrong Nov 1].
- outcomeCounts -> wrong 1; outcomeNotes hands the judge 'wrong note'; quality report -> right 1.

## Expected impact
The learning loop's memory inverts the person's latest judgement for every item rated twice before a store's first sync (a new machine, a CI runner, a cleared store). Fix: order by `recorded_at DESC, id DESC` in reflect.mjs (as quality.mjs does), and make the mock return newest-first without outcomes_since.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the 'latest rating' is the newest recorded one everywhere.
Before: probe - outcomeCounts {right:0, wrong:1}, outcomeNotes [wrong note], qualityReport outcomes {right:1, wrong:0} for the same card.
After: all three report `right` (recorded_at order is independent of insert order).
Method: probe - scratch script outside the repo fed ingestReflect the Forge first-page order and read the three readers; the fix was walked, not built.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: Probe: `reflect.outcomeCounts {"right":0,"partly":0,"wrong":1}`, `reflect.outcomeNotes [{"rating":"wrong","note":"wrong note"}]`, `quality outcomes [{"right":1,"partly":0,"wrong":0}]`. skill/scripts/lib/reflect.mjs:184 `WHERE p.lens = ? AND o.id = (SELECT MAX(o2.id) FROM outcomes o2 WHERE o2.fp = o.fp)`; forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:101 `ORDER BY recorded_at DESC, ref DESC LIMIT ${OUTCOMES_MAX}`; skill/scripts/lib/quality.mjs:86 `ORDER BY o.recorded_at DESC, o.id DESC LIMIT 1`.

title: Accept-claim race and stale-claim takeover are untested
body:
## Summary
The claim that stops a double click or a second agent from creating two Jira issues has no test for its refusal or its stale-claim takeover.

## Description
forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:168 claims with `accept_claim IS NULL OR accept_claim < ?` (CLAIM_MS = 120_000, forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:34) and refuses with "an accept of ... is already in progress" (forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:173). `grep -n "in progress\|CLAIM_MS" forge/test/*.mjs` finds neither. Only the release after a Jira failure is asserted (forge/test/core.test.mjs:145). The helpers already have a controllable clock (forge/test/helpers.mjs:185) and a statement hook (`before`, helpers.mjs CountingDb), so both cases can be written as they stand.

## Flow
- accept A claims and awaits createIssue
- accept B arrives: it should be refused with in progress, and no second issue is created
- A crashes; after 120 s a new accept takes over the stale claim

## Expected impact
Add two tests: (1) a second accept while the first holds the claim is refused and jira.created stays 1; (2) d.clock.tick(CLAIM_MS + 1) lets a new accept take over.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the duplicate-issue guard is under test.
Before: 0 tests reach verdicts.mjs:173.
After: refusal and takeover both asserted.
Method: simulation - walked both paths with the existing clock and before-hook helpers.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:173 `throw new AppError('bad-input', `an accept of ${p.ref} is already in progress; reload in a minute`);`; `grep -n "in progress\|accept_claim\|CLAIM_MS" forge/test/*.mjs` -> only core.test.mjs:145 `assert.equal(proposalRows(d)[0].accept_claim, null, 'the claim is released');`

title: Test that every UI call() key is registered and allowed for its module
body:
## Summary
Nothing checks the Custom UI's call() keys against the Forge resolver registration (index.js KEYS) and MODULE_KEYS; the two dev bridges and the local server do not apply module gating at all, so a key that works in every dev mode can still answer an error in Forge.

## Description
The UI calls 21 keys (grep of call('...') in forge/static/app/src). Registration is a hand list (forge/src/index.js:90-92) and the gate is MODULE_KEYS (forge/src/core/app.mjs:304-309, resolverAllowed :312). The fixture bridge dispatches any handler by key (src/dev/bridge.js:306-311), http-bridge sends `module` only for the panel (src/dev/http-bridge.js:18), and tools/local-forge.mjs:236-237 calls forge.resolver without resolverAllowed. access.test.mjs:144-147 asserts four hand-picked pairs. The already-known missing byline.draftFix in KEYS is one instance of this gap; this proposal is the guard, not that fix: a test that scans static/app/src for call('<key>') per route, maps the route to its module (router.jsx MODULES/PAGES) and asserts KEYS.includes(key) && resolverAllowed(module, key).

## Flow
- Add a resolver key in core/app.mjs and a call() in a new route
- Fixture and dev:local both work
- Forge answers 'is not available from this Dowser view' or no function; only a deploy finds it

## Expected impact
The registration and gating door is checked from ground truth (the UI source) on every npm test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - UI keys verified against registration
Before: 0 tests derive from the UI's call sites; 3 dev paths skip gating
After: 1 test over all call sites; a missing key fails CI
Method: probe - grep of call sites, KEYS and tests; the scan would be written in the build
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/index.js:90 `const KEYS = ['inbox.list', 'proposal.get', ...` ; forge/src/core/app.mjs:312 `export const resolverAllowed = (moduleKey, key) => ...` ; forge/static/app/src/dev/bridge.js:309 `const h = handlers[key];` (no module check) ; src/dev/http-bridge.js:18 `...(surface() === 'panel' ? { module: 'dowser-evidence' } : {})` ; tools/local-forge.mjs:237 `return json(200, await forge.resolver(b.key, b.payload ?? {}, via));` ; forge/test/access.test.mjs:144-147 four literal resolverAllowed pairs

title: Make bulk reject and snooze set-based: 50 refs cost 550 SQL statements
body:
## Summary
A bulk reject or snooze of one inbox page (50 cards) runs 550 Forge SQL statements, about 16-33 s at the 30-60 ms per statement store.mjs assumes, so it can pass the 25 s resolver limit and leave a half-decided batch.

## Description
app.mjs:239 checks each ref one by one (openRefs app.mjs:74: findProposal + needInbox per ref), then verdicts.mjs:206 openItems reads each ref again, and verdicts.mjs:226 decideAll runs decide (verdicts.mjs:109: UPDATE, SELECT, appendVerdict SELECT, counter SELECT+UPDATE, INSERT) and cardOf (cards.mjs:118: getInbox + evidenceOf) per card. openItems allows 200 refs (verdicts.mjs:208), i.e. ~2200 statements. The push path was made set-based for exactly this reason (store.mjs:70 "bulk work is a few multi-row statements, not one per row"); the decision path was not. The UI selects many cards and sends them in one call (static/app/src/routes/inbox/useVerdicts.js:81).

## Flow
- person selects a page of cards and presses r
- verdict.reject with 50 refs
- 550 sequential statements
- invocation killed past 25 s: some cards rejected, the UI says the batch is back in the list

## Expected impact
Bulk triage, the inbox's main gesture, stays inside the invocation limit; no half-applied batch the UI misreports.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the call fits Forge's resolver time limit
Before: 550 statements for 50 refs (11 per ref), measured
After: about a dozen statements for 50 refs: one IN read of the refs, one IN read of their inboxes, one CAS UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (...) AND status = 'open', one seq block (nextCounterBlock), one multi-row verdict INSERT, one evidenceOfMany
Method: probe - scratch script outside the repo ran the real core over forge/test/helpers.mjs countingDb: push 50, then runResolver verdict.reject with the 50 refs -> 550 statements; the After is a design, not built (ideas-only)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: "reject50 statements 550 50"; forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:208 `if (refs.length > 200) throw ...`; forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:229 `for (const p of items) {` -> `cards.push(await cardOf(deps.db, await decide(deps, p, d, who)))`; forge/src/core/app.mjs:74 `if (Array.isArray(refs)) for (const r of refs) if (typeof r === 'string') await acc.proposal(r);`; forge/src/core/store.mjs:70 "Every statement is one Forge SQL request (30-60 ms), so bulk work is a few multi-row statements"
impact_why: bulk reject/snooze of a page is the main triage gesture; past 25 s it half-applies and the UI reports it failed

title: One failing requirements file throws away every pip-audit finding
body:
## Summary
`pipAudit` runs one pip-audit per requirements file, but the first target that fails returns `skipped` with `findings: []`, discarding what earlier targets found and never running the later ones. A broken `requirements-dev.txt` hides a real advisory in `requirements.txt`.

## Description
skill/scripts/lib/deps.mjs:379-385 loops the targets and returns from inside the loop on the first unusable report (skill/scripts/lib/deps.mjs:383). Targets are sorted, so `requirements-dev.txt` runs before `requirements.txt`. The module header promises an auditor that fails is "reported as skipped, never as no vulnerabilities" (skill/scripts/lib/deps.mjs:4-5); here the tool is reported skipped, which is honest, but the security-cra lens then has no dep ref to cite for the advisory that was found, and verify drops any card citing it (`ref-not-ingested`, skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:219).

## Flow
- dir has requirements-dev.txt (unresolvable pin) and requirements.txt (flask==0.1)
- pip-audit on dev fails -> return skipped, findings []
- requirements.txt never audited; 0 dep refs cached

## Expected impact
Per-target reports: a failed target is listed as skipped with its manifest, the others still run and cache their findings (state `partial` or one report per manifest).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one bad manifest does not hide the others' advisories
Before: probe with an injected System (dev file exits 2, requirements.txt returns PYSEC-2019-179) -> pip-audit skipped, refs 0
After: refs 1 (requirements.txt#flask@0.1) plus a skipped entry for requirements-dev.txt (simulation of the per-target loop)
Method: probe - scratch script called the real runDeps with a fake System and a temp dir outside the repo
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/deps.mjs:383 `if (!report) return { report: { tool, state: 'skipped', reason: \`${t.manifest}: ${why ?? (firstLine(r.stderr) || 'output was not JSON')}\` }, findings: [] };`; probe: `[{"tool":"pip-audit","state":"skipped","reason":"requirements-dev.txt: ERROR: Could not resolve pytest==1"}] refs 0`
impact_why: A known vulnerable dependency goes uncited by the security lens whenever any sibling requirements file fails to resolve

title: A lost migration checkpoint wedges every later migration for good
body:
## Summary
The non-idempotent migrations (CREATE INDEX, ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN) re-run after a failed checkpoint and then fail every time, so no later migration ever runs again.

## Description
@forge/sql 4.0.9 MigrationRunner.run() (node_modules/@forge/sql/out/migration.js) runs `executeDDL(statement)` and only then INSERTs the name into __migrations; a failed INSERT throws MigrationCheckPointError with the DDL already applied. forge/src/adapters/forge-sql.mjs:50-52 enqueues every MIGRATIONS entry and calls run(). In forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs, v004/v005/v007/v010/v014/v029 are `CREATE INDEX` without IF NOT EXISTS (e.g. forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:78) and v016-v022/v025/v026 are `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` (forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:199). On the next run the unrecorded statement executes again, TiDB answers duplicate column/key name, run() throws MigrationExecutionError and stops before every later name. The file is append-only (forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:4), so the shipped statements cannot simply gain IF NOT EXISTS. Then forge/src/index.js:47-56 withSchema retries the same failing run on every call that hits the missing column.

## Flow
- v016 ALTER succeeds; the INSERT INTO __migrations request fails (one HTTP POST each, forge-sql.mjs header)
- next migrate: v016 is not in __migrations, ALTER runs again, Duplicate column name, MigrationExecutionError
- v017..v031 never run; any query on verdicts.snooze_until is ER_BAD_FIELD_ERROR
- every resolver/tool call answers unavailable "storage is not ready" until someone edits __migrations by hand

## Expected impact
An installation that loses one checkpoint request stops working until someone fixes it by hand. The fix: in runMigrations, treat a MigrationExecutionError whose cause is errno 1060/1061 (duplicate column / key name) as already applied, record the name, and run the rest.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a transient checkpoint failure no longer bricks the schema.
Before: a re-run of an applied ALTER/CREATE INDEX fails forever (read from out/migration.js run()).
After: the duplicate-DDL error is recorded as applied and later migrations run.
Method: simulation - walked three cases (checkpoint lost on v016 ALTER; on v029 CREATE INDEX; on v031 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, which is already safe); no TiDB reachable to probe.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: node_modules/@forge/sql/out/migration.js run(): `await this.sqlClient.executeDDL(migration.statement);` then `throw new errors_1.MigrationCheckPointError(...)` around INSERT_SCHEMA_VERSION_QUERY; forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:78 `{ name: 'v004_proposals_status_ix', statement: 'CREATE INDEX ix_proposals_status ON proposals (project_key, status, last_push_at)' }`; forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:199 `{ name: 'v016_proposals_snooze_until', statement: 'ALTER TABLE proposals ADD COLUMN snooze_until VARCHAR(10)' }`; forge/src/adapters/forge-sql.mjs:51-52 `for (const m of MIGRATIONS) migrationRunner.enqueue(m.name, m.statement); return migrationRunner.run();`
impact_why: One lost request leaves an installation permanently unavailable; recovery needs a manual SQL edit

title: Trust window counts decision transitions, not decided items
body:
## Summary
The earn window is meant to be 'the last 20 human-decided items' (docs/contracts/scan-finding-1.md:71-72) but trust.mjs counts every human transition to accepted/rejected/snoozed, so one card that is snoozed, resurfaces and is accepted fills two of the 20 slots, once as a disagreement and once as an agreement.

## Description
- skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:46-56 `decisions()` selects `FROM transitions t JOIN proposals p ... WHERE t.to_status IN ('accepted','rejected','snoozed')` - one row per transition, not per fp.
- skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:66-68 `windowStats` slices the last WINDOW of that list.
- skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:85-90 makes repeated decisions on one fp ordinary: pushed -> snoozed -> verified/candidate -> ... -> accepted, and rejected -> candidate -> ... -> rejected.
- Contract: 'agree with the human verdicts on >= 90 % of its last 20 human-decided items (min 20...)'.

## Flow
- Card A predicted accept; a person snoozes it (defer, disagrees), it resurfaces, a person accepts it (agrees).
- trustReport: n = 2, agreement = 0.5 for that slice, from one item.
- A slice of 12 items with 8 snooze-then-accept cycles reaches n = 20 with 60 % agreement - neither the min-20 nor the agreement matches the contract's meaning.

## Expected impact
The earn rule reaches 'min 20' early on churny slices and its agreement mixes intermediate snoozes with final verdicts. Fix: per slice keep the latest human decision per fp in the window (and keep the reversal check per transition).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the window measures what the contract names.
Before: one card, two decisions -> slice n = 2, agreement 0.5 (probe).
After: n = 1, agreement 1.0 (the latest decision of that item).
Method: probe - scratch script drove the real store: snooze, resurface, accept one predicted-accept card, then trustReport; the per-item fix was walked, not built.
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: Probe: `after accept [{"slice":"technical|doc-drift|-|S","level":0,..."n":2,"agreement":0.5}]` with transitions for fp 152582c2054ffec4: `{id:6,to_status:snoozed,by:human:owner}`, `{id:9,to_status:accepted,by:human:owner}`; skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:47-50 `SELECT t.id, t.fp, t.to_status ... FROM transitions t JOIN proposals p ON p.fp = t.fp WHERE t.to_status IN ('accepted', 'rejected', 'snoozed')`; contract docs/contracts/scan-finding-1.md:71-72 `>= 90 % of its last 20 human-decided items (min 20; ...)`.
impact_why: The earn gate's n and agreement are measured over transitions; churny slices earn or fail L1 on the wrong evidence.

title: Mock Forge MCP files records and trust that real Forge refuses
body:
## Summary
tools/mock-forge-mcp.mjs stands in for the Forge resolver in the skill's end-to-end tests, but it skips the validation the real tools run, so a producer bug that Forge would refuse passes every mock-backed test.

## Description
- Push: forge/src/core/push.mjs:119 runs `validateCandidate(cand, { wire: true })` (score range, score_parts keys, lens, kind, sizes) and forge/src/core/push.mjs:134 refuses an fp that does not hash from its identity. The mock (tools/mock-forge-mcp.mjs:315-317) checks only fp, title, evidence and status.
- Reflect: forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:88 `await needInbox(db, projectKey)` answers unknown-project; the mock's `project(b, key)` (tools/mock-forge-mcp.mjs:181) creates the project silently.
- Trust: forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:149-163 caps slices at TRUST_SLICES_MAX (200) and checks every slice's level/ceiling/start/n/agreement; the mock (tools/mock-forge-mcp.mjs:471) checks the events cap only.
- Empty `rules_json`: Forge treats '' as no offers (forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:86); the mock's jsonArray throws bad-input.
- Both sides can share the checks: validateCandidate and fingerprint already live in skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs and fingerprint.mjs, which the mock imports from (tools/mock-forge-mcp.mjs:49-50).

## Flow
- A change makes propose store score 0 or a wrong fp -> the mock-backed e2e push says `created` -> Forge in production answers `refused` for every card.
- A store grows past 200 trust slices -> mock reflect sync passes -> Forge refuses the whole reflect sync, so rules and outcomes stop syncing too.

## Expected impact
The e2e tests (skill/scripts/tests/local-forge-e2e.test.mjs, sync-mcp.test.mjs) prove the contract only where the mock enforces it. Fix: run the shared validateCandidate({wire:true}) + fingerprint check in the mock push, needInbox in reflect_sync, and the slice checks in trust.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the mock refuses what Forge refuses.
Before: probe against callTool: push of {fp:'zzzz', lens:'nope', score:0} -> `created` DW-1; reflect_sync on an unknown project -> {rules:[],outcomes:[]}; trust_json with level 9 or 201 slices -> accepted.
After: the same four calls answer refused / unknown-project / bad-input, as forge/src/core/push.mjs and reflect.mjs do.
Method: probe - a scratch script outside the repo imported callTool and ran the calls; Forge's answers read from its code (no Forge runtime here).
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: Probe output: `reflect unknown {"rules":[],"outcomes":[]}`, `trust bad slice {"rules":[],"outcomes":[]}`, `trust 201 slices {"rules":[],"outcomes":[]}`, `push bad fp/score {"results":[{"fp":"zzzz","result":"created","external_ref":"DW-1"...}]}`, `rules empty string ERR bad-input: rules_json does not parse as JSON`. Forge: forge/src/core/push.mjs:119 `const v = validateCandidate(cand, { wire: true });`, forge/src/core/push.mjs:134 `if (fp !== cand.fp) return { ok: false, ...`, forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:88 `await needInbox(db, projectKey);`, forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:149 `if (t.slices.length > TRUST_SLICES_MAX || t.events.length > TRUST_EVENTS_MAX)`.
impact_why: Mock-backed e2e tests pass on records Forge refuses; a producer regression reaches production unseen.

title: Log the failing migration's name when storage is not ready
body:
## Summary
safe() logs only the error class name, so a wedged migration leaves just "storage not ready (MigrationExecutionError)" in the logs, with no migration name, no cause and no hint.

## Description
forge/src/index.js:83 logs `dowser: storage not ready (<e.name>)` for every non-consent error that escapes, and answers "try again in a minute" (forge/src/index.js:84). @forge/sql MigrationExecutionError and MigrationCheckPointError carry migrationName, migrationsYetToRun and cause (node_modules/@forge/sql/out/errors.d.ts), and ForgeSQLAPIError carries code and responseDetails.traceId. None of these contain user content, so logging them is safe under the "no body in errors" rule (forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:42-43).

## Flow
- a migration fails inside withSchema
- the log reads "storage not ready (MigrationExecutionError)"
- the operator cannot tell which migration, or whether it is transient, without redeploying with more logging

## Expected impact
Log one JSON line with name, code, migrationName, migrationsYetToRun.length and the traceId. Then the wedge in forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs is visible from `forge logs`.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - diagnosability of storage failures.
Before: error class name only (index.js:83).
After: the failing migration name, error code and trace id.
Method: simulation - walked MigrationExecutionError, ForgeSQLAPIError (ER_NO_SUCH_TABLE), and a plain Error; all fields are metadata.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/index.js:83 `console.error(`dowser: storage not ready (${String(/** @type {any} */ (e)?.name ?? typeof e)})`);`; node_modules/@forge/sql/out/errors.d.ts `export declare class MigrationExecutionError extends ForgeSQLError { readonly migrationName: string; readonly migrationsYetToRun: string[]; readonly cause?: Error`
impact_why: Turns a silent outage into a named one in forge logs

title: Nothing enforces the append-only migrations rule
body:
## Summary
migrations.mjs says "never edit a migration that has shipped", but no test pins the shipped statements, so an edit passes on a fresh SQLite and never reaches an installed database.

## Description
forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:4 "Append only: never edit a migration that has shipped." The tests rebuild the schema from MIGRATIONS on every run (forge/test/helpers.mjs:28), so an edited v003 statement is green in CI. In production the runner skips any name already in __migrations, so the edit never runs there and the two schemas split. No test asserts names are unique and ordered either (`grep -n "v0[0-9][0-9]_" forge/test/*.mjs` finds only direction.test.mjs:105 using v015 by name).

## Flow
- someone adds a column to v003_proposals instead of appending v032
- tests pass (fresh SQLite gets the column)
- installed sites never get it, and the first query on it is ER_BAD_FIELD forever (the migration runner sees v003 as done)

## Expected impact
Add a test with a frozen digest per shipped migration name (sha256 of the statement) plus a check that names are unique and strictly increasing. A new migration adds a line; an edited one fails with "append a new migration instead".

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the append-only rule is enforced.
Before: an edited shipped migration is green.
After: it fails with a pointer to the rule.
Method: simulation - walked append (passes), edit of v003 (fails), duplicate name (fails).
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:4 `// tests run the same statements on node:sqlite. Append only: never edit a migration that has shipped.`; forge/test/helpers.mjs:28 `for (const m of MIGRATIONS) raw.exec(m.statement);`
impact_why: Turns a silent prod/test schema split into a failing test

title: Info toasts vanish after 5 s with no pause, taking the new Jira issue link along
body:
## Summary
Only undo toasts pause on hover/focus; info toasts dismiss on a fixed 5 s timer. The Accept notice carries the only link to the just-created Jira issue, and it disappears while a keyboard user is still tabbing to it (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing adjustable).

## Description
Toast.jsx:7-11 starts a NOTICE_MS timer for every 'info' toast (useCommitWindow.js:10 NOTICE_MS = 5000); pause/resume are wired only when `undoable` (Toast.jsx:17-18). The toast region sits at the end of <main> (routes/inbox/index.jsx:171 renders ToastRegion last), so reaching it by Tab from the list takes many stops. The accept notice embeds the issue link (routes/inbox/InboxDialogs.jsx:25); after the dialog closes focus goes to the next row, and the card leaves the list, so the toast is the one place the link to the new issue appears on the page.

## Flow
- Accept DW-7 with Ctrl+Enter: toast 'DW-7 accepted as SHOP-123' with a link
- Keyboard user starts tabbing toward the toast region
- At 5 s the toast and its link are removed, even if the link has focus

## Expected impact
The new issue's link stays reachable; timed content meets WCAG 2.2.1.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a notice holding a link never times out under focus or hover
Before: info toast removed at 5 s regardless of hover/focus
After: info toasts pause on hover/focus like undo toasts (or a toast with interactive content does not auto-dismiss)
Method: simulation - walked mouse-hover, keyboard-focus and idle cases through Toast.jsx timers; no browser in a read-only scout
Result: better

() => onPause(toast.id) : undefined} ...` :18 `onFocus={undoable ? title: UX error-string grep misses every template-literal throw

## Summary

title: Accept orphans its Jira issue and files a duplicate when the decide step fails
body:
## Summary
Accept creates the Jira issue first, then records the decision. A non-AppError failure of that record step (a Forge SQL error, or the function timing out) is rethrown raw: the caller sees a generic error with no issue key, the claim expires after 2 minutes, and the next accept creates a second issue.

## Description
verdicts.mjs:182 createIssue; verdicts.mjs:191 decide; the catch at verdicts.mjs:194-196 adds the "Jira issue X was created; link or delete it by hand" note only to an AppError and rethrows anything else, which answer() (app.mjs:155-164) turns into "Dowser hit an unexpected error; try again". Nothing records the created key before decide, so after CLAIM_MS (verdicts.mjs:34, 120 s) the claim CAS at verdicts.mjs:168 succeeds again and a retry calls createIssue a second time. The comment at verdicts.mjs:164 says the claim exists so "a double click or a second agent cannot create two issues".

## Flow
- person accepts DW-n
- Jira issue SHOP-41 created
- decide UPDATE hits a transient SQL error, or the invocation is cut
- UI: unexpected error, try again
- two minutes later the retry creates SHOP-42; SHOP-41 has no Dowser record

## Expected impact
One accepted card maps to one Jira issue even across failures; an orphan is either linked or named to the person.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one issue per accept
Before: raw throw after createIssue: no key reported, duplicate on retry after 120 s (re-read of the code)
After: the issue key is stamped on the claimed row before decide (or the catch reports it for every error), and a retry that finds a stamped key finishes the decide instead of calling createIssue
Method: simulation - three cases walked against verdicts.mjs:150-197: AppError from decide (note added, ok), SQL error from decide (raw, no key, retry duplicates), timeout after createIssue (no catch runs, claim expires, retry duplicates); a probe needs a fault-injecting Db not built in an ideas-only round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:194 `} catch (e) {` / :195 `if (e instanceof AppError) throw new AppError(e.code, `${e.message}. Jira issue ${issue.key} was created; link or delete it by hand`);` / :196 `throw e;`; forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:168 `UPDATE proposals SET accept_claim = ? WHERE id = ? AND status = 'open' AND (accept_claim IS NULL OR accept_claim < ?)`

title: Test Db port is transactional; the production port is not
body:
## Summary
The SQLite test port wraps tx() in BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, while forgeDb.tx just runs fn. A core change that leans on rollback passes every test and leaves partial writes on Forge.

## Description
forge/test/helpers.mjs:46-48 `raw.exec('BEGIN') ... raw.exec('ROLLBACK')`; forge/src/adapters/forge-sql.mjs:42-43 "Not atomic on Forge SQL ... runs `fn` as is". forge/src/core/ports.mjs:12-13 states the core "never relies on it for correctness", and the one caller today (forge/src/core/verdicts.mjs:113 decide) catches its own appendVerdict failure, so it holds now. But no test enforces the claim: every test runs with real rollback. The port is also a hazard the other way. SQLite refuses a nested or interleaved BEGIN ("cannot start a transaction within a transaction"), so a concurrent-decide test would fail on the test port for a reason production does not have.

## Flow
- a future change throws after a second write inside db.tx
- tests: ROLLBACK undoes the first write, assertions pass
- Forge: the first write stays, and the item is half-decided

## Expected impact
Make the default test tx non-atomic (match production: `async tx(fn) { return fn(); }`). Keep an opt-in atomic variant only for a test that names why it needs one.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - tests run under the production guarantee.
Before: the tests have rollback; production does not (helpers.mjs:46 vs forge-sql.mjs:43).
After: a reliance on rollback fails a test.
Method: simulation - walked decide() today (unaffected: its only post-write throw is caught), a hypothetical throw-after-write, and two concurrent tx calls on the SQLite port.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/test/helpers.mjs:46-48 `async tx(fn) { raw.exec('BEGIN'); try { const out = await fn(); raw.exec('COMMIT'); return out; } catch (e) { raw.exec('ROLLBACK'); throw e; }`; forge/src/adapters/forge-sql.mjs:42-43 `// Not atomic on Forge SQL (see the header); runs `fn` as is.\n  async tx(fn) { return fn(); },`
impact_why: Closes the one place where the tests are stronger than production

title: Rule offers count items the person later accepted
body:
## Summary
`offerRules` clusters every item that was EVER rejected, read from the transition history, without checking where the item ended. An item rejected once, resurfaced with stronger evidence and then accepted still counts toward a 'Do not propose ... about <token>' rule - so the learning loop can offer to suppress exactly the topic the person just accepted.

## Description
- skill/scripts/lib/memory.mjs:365-366 `SELECT DISTINCT p.fp, p.lens, p.topic, p.title, t.reason FROM transitions t JOIN proposals p ON p.fp = t.fp WHERE t.to_status = 'rejected' AND t.reason IS NOT NULL` - no condition on p.status.
- skill/scripts/lib/memory.mjs:399 the draft text then claims `rejected ${g.fps.length}x as ${g.reason}`.
- The resurfacing rule (skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:626-632) exists precisely so a rejected item can come back and be accepted; skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:90 `rejected -> candidate`.
- Accepted rules then reach the judge as standing instructions (skill/scripts/lib/memory.mjs:199 rules in contextPack).

## Flow
- Three doc-drift items about 'webhook retry' are rejected as not-worth-it.
- Item 1 resurfaces with code + doc evidence and the person accepts it.
- `rules offer` -> 'Do not propose doc-drift items about webhook (rejected 3x as not-worth-it)', cluster fps include the accepted item.
- If the runner accepts the offer, future webhook cards are suppressed against the person's latest decision.

## Expected impact
A standing rule contradicts a later acceptance; the person is the gate, but the offer's count and titles mislead them. Fix: count an fp only when its current status is still rejected (or its latest human decision is a rejection), so the example becomes 2 items and no offer.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a rule offer reflects the person's latest decisions.
Before: probe - offers [{text:'Do not propose doc-drift items about webhook (rejected 3x as not-worth-it)', fps:3, has_accepted:true}].
After: the cluster holds 2 fps (< RULE_THRESHOLD 3) and no offer is made; three items still rejected still produce the offer.
Method: probe - scratch script outside the repo drove propose/move/offerRules on a temp store; the status filter was walked, not built.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: Probe output: `status of item 0 accepted` then `[{"text":"Do not propose doc-drift items about webhook (rejected 3x as not-worth-it)","fps":3,"has_accepted":true}]`. skill/scripts/lib/memory.mjs:366 `WHERE t.to_status = 'rejected' AND t.reason IS NOT NULL ORDER BY p.fp`.
impact_why: The learning loop offers a suppression rule built partly from items the person accepted after resurfacing.

title: The real migrate-and-retry path in index.js has no test
body:
## Summary
withSchema/ensureSchema in forge/src/index.js run on every live call that hits a missing table, but no test runs them. The one test that covers the path swaps in its own ensureSchema.

## Description
forge/test/sample.test.mjs:350-355 replaces d.ensureSchema with a test-written closure ("if (migrations > 0 ...) return false; migrations += 1"). It restates the rule instead of running the shipped one (forge/src/index.js:32-38, :47-56). forge/test/direction.test.mjs:103 and core.test.mjs:387-399 only prove the error escapes answer() "so index.js migrates and retries". The retry itself is never run. The adds-before-await defect filed in forge-backend-shell (forge/src/index.js:35, :53) survives because of this gap. index.js imports @forge/api, @forge/resolver and @forge/sql, so a test needs module mocks (node --test --experimental-test-module-mocks, mock.module, Node >= 22.3).

## Flow
- a call hits ER_NO_SUCH_TABLE
- the test fake migrates once and returns true; the real code adds to migrated first
- a failing migration in production disables the retry; the test cannot see it

## Expected impact
Pull the retry into a pure helper (e.g. core/schema.mjs: makeSchemaGuard(runMigrations, installationId)) and test it directly: a transient failure then a retry, two concurrent callers, two installations. index.js keeps only the wiring.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the shipped retry rule is under test.
Before: 0 tests execute forge/src/index.js (it is not imported by any test: grep of test imports lists no ../src/index.js).
After: the retry rule runs in a test, including the failure case.
Method: simulation - walked the three cases against the current index.js lines.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/test/sample.test.mjs:350-351 `d.ensureSchema = async (/** @type {unknown} */ e) => { if (migrations > 0 || !/no such table/i.test(String(/** @type {any} */ (e)?.message))) return false;`; test import census (grep -ho "from '../src/[^']*'" forge/test/*.mjs): no ../src/index.js and no ../src/adapters/*
impact_why: The only path that heals a minor-deploy schema gap is exercised by a re-implementation, not the code

title: Schema retry marks an installation migrated before the migration succeeds
body:
## Summary
ensureSchema and withSchema add the installation to `migrated` before awaiting runMigrations, so one failed or in-flight migration disables the retry for the rest of the warm runtime.

## Description
forge/src/index.js:34-36 (ensureSchema) and forge/src/index.js:52-54 (withSchema) both do `migrated.add(inst); await runMigrations();`. If runMigrations throws (a transient Forge SQL 5xx), the set still holds the installation; every later call that hits the missing table sees `migrated.has(inst)` and rethrows (forge/src/index.js:34, :52), answering "storage is not ready" until the runtime recycles or the daily trigger runs. A second call that arrives while the first is still migrating also fails right away instead of waiting. The two functions are a pair holding the same rule twice.

## Flow
- call A hits ER_NO_SUCH_TABLE, adds inst, runMigrations rejects (HTTP 503)
- call B hits the same table: migrated.has(inst) is true, so it rethrows, safe() answers unavailable
- every call until the runtime dies or dowser-migrate-daily runs fails the same way

## Expected impact
Keep one per-installation promise (Map inst -> Promise), delete it on rejection, and have concurrent callers await it. That folds ensureSchema and withSchema into one helper.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed in-request migration is retried on the next call; concurrent calls wait instead of failing.
Before: one rejection blocks retries for the runtime lifetime (forge/src/index.js:35, :53 add before await).
After: a rejection clears the entry; the next call migrates again.
Method: simulation - walked (1) transient failure then retry, (2) two concurrent calls, (3) success path unchanged; index.js imports @forge/api so no unit probe without module mocks.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/index.js:34-36 `if (migrated.has(inst) || !isSchemaBehind(e)) return false; migrated.add(inst); await runMigrations();`; forge/src/index.js:52-54 `if (migrated.has(inst) || !isSchemaBehind(e)) throw e; migrated.add(inst); await runMigrations();`
impact_why: A transient SQL failure during a minor-deploy migration makes the app unavailable for the runtime lifetime

title: Issue-property backfill blocks behind 50 permanently failing rows
body:
## Summary
The daily backfill retries the oldest 50 unwritten issue properties; a write that always fails (issue deleted, moved, or no permission) is never stamped, so 50 such rows block every newer one forever. Without the property, the delivery triggers never fire for those issues.

## Description
issue-property.mjs:87-92 selects `issue_prop_at IS NULL ... ORDER BY decided_at, id LIMIT 50`; writeIssueProperty returns `failed` without stamping (issue-property.mjs:75), so the same rows come back next day. The issue-event trigger filters on the property (manifest.yml dowser-issue-events: `event.runtime.issue.properties['dowser'].ref != null`), so an accepted card whose property never lands gets no delivery truth (delivery.mjs:67). Accepted sample cards whose issues a person later deleted are a ready source of permanent failures.

## Flow
- 50 accepts whose Jira issues were later deleted
- each daily run: the same 50 fail
- a new accept whose write failed transiently is never retried
- its issue gets no delivery events

## Expected impact
Every retryable property write lands within a day; delivery truth covers every accepted card.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - backfill progress
Before: oldest-first LIMIT 50 with no failure mark: head-of-line blocking (re-read)
After: a failure count or last-try stamp (skip after N tries, or order by last attempt) so newer rows advance; a 404 marks the row done
Method: simulation - walked 3 cases through backfillIssueProperties: 0 permanent failures (all advance), 10 (40 newer per day advance), 50 (none advance, ever); not probed because the fake Jira has no per-key failure switch
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/issue-property.mjs:91 `ORDER BY decided_at, id LIMIT ${BACKFILL_MAX}`; forge/src/core/issue-property.mjs:75 `return 'failed';` (no stamp); forge/manifest.yml dowser-issue-events filter `event.runtime.issue.properties['dowser'].ref != null`
impact_why: silently stops the property backfill and delivery truth for every later failed write

title: Wire check accepts a score its own breakdown does not produce
body:
## Summary
The shared wire validation (skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs, copied to forge/src/shared/model.mjs) checks only that `score` is in (0, 100] and that `score_parts` has five numeric/string keys. It accepts any `formula` string and a score that its own breakdown, and the record's own impact, cannot produce. The Forge inbox sorts on that number (forge/src/core/cards.mjs:198), so one bad producer outranks every honest card.

## Description
- skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:523 `if (o.score !== undefined && !(typeof o.score === 'number' && ... o.score > 0 && o.score <= 100))` - the only score check.
- skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:530 `if (!str(sp.formula)) return 'score_parts.formula:required';` - any string passes; docs/contracts/scan-finding-1.md:36 says a formula change 'is scan-score/2, never an edit', which only helps if a consumer can tell the two apart.
- No check ties score_parts.impact to the record's impact, or score to round1(10*impact*confidence_w/effort_div*risk_factor).
- forge/src/core/cards.mjs:198 `... CASE WHEN score IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, score DESC` - the inbox order.

## Flow
- A record with impact 2, confidence high, size S (scan-score/1 = 12.8) arrives with score 95 and score_parts {impact: 9, confidence_w: 7, effort_div: 0.1, risk_factor: 3, formula: 'made-up'}.
- validateCandidate(wire) -> ok; Forge stores it; the inbox lists it first.
- With the check: refused `score_parts.formula:must be scan-score/1` / `score:does not match score_parts`.

## Expected impact
The contract's 'stored by the producer; consumers sort by it' only holds if the store refuses an inconsistent number. Fix: require formula === FORMULA, score_parts.impact === impact, and score === round1 of the parts (verifying the stored breakdown, not re-ranking), in the shared computedProblem so both sides gain it via sync-shared.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - an inconsistent score cannot reach the inbox order.
Before: probe - validateCandidate({...card, impact 2, score 95, score_parts formula 'made-up', confidence_w 7}, {wire: true}) -> ok:true.
After: the same record is refused; the four contract reference values and every honest record still pass (scanScore of their own parts reproduces them).
Method: probe - ran the shared validateCandidate from a scratch command; the added check was simulated on the reference values.
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: Probe: `made-up {"ok":true,"value":{...}}` for score 95 with score_parts {impact:9, confidence_w:7, effort_div:0.1, risk_factor:3, formula:'made-up'} on an impact-2 card. skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:530 `if (!str(sp.formula)) return 'score_parts.formula:required';`; forge/src/core/cards.mjs:198 `CASE WHEN score IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, score DESC`.
impact_why: A wrong or foreign-formula score is stored and leads the inbox order; the contract's formula versioning is unenforced.
predicted_why: no precedent (door unreachable, digest absent); contract says consumers never recompute, so verifying the breakdown is a contract call

title: One hidden or deleted issue key fails the whole status batch
body:
## Summary
The port promises that a key the user cannot see is simply absent, but issueStatuses sends `key in (...)` JQL, which Jira refuses outright when any listed key does not exist or is not visible.

## Description
forge/src/core/ports.mjs:49 says issueStatuses "answers only the keys Jira returned (a missing key is one the user cannot browse, or gone)", and forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:171-172 repeats it. The adapter posts a `key in (...)` JQL (forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:182) for chunks of 50. Jira JQL validation answers 400 ("An issue with key ... does not exist for field key") for an unknown or invisible key, and json() throws (forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:51). candidatesOf catches it and drops ALL statuses (forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:327), so every candidate shows "unknown". Deleted issues are a designed case (the dowser-issue-deleted trigger, forge/manifest.yml:273), and accepts may target projects other viewers cannot browse (atlassian.mjs:171), so this is the normal case, not an edge.

## Flow
- DW-1 accepted into SHOP-1, DW-2 into a private project HR-7
- a viewer without HR access opens Learning
- JQL key in (SHOP-1,HR-7) answers 400, so the whole chunk throws
- SHOP-1 shows "unknown" too, and the done flag is false for every candidate

## Expected impact
Use POST /rest/api/3/issue/bulkfetch (issueIdsOrKeys, fields [status]), which returns the visible issues and lists the rest under issueErrors. The other way is to pass the query with validation off. Either makes the port contract true.

Claim: quality - statuses survive one unreadable key.

title: A bug in dowser.mjs is reported as "store unavailable", its stack dropped
body:
## Summary
Give non-DowserError exceptions their own error code (`internal`) and print the stack on stderr, so a programming error is not read by the agent as a connection or store outage.

## Description
skill/scripts/dowser.mjs:620-621 maps every exception that is not a DowserError to exit 3 with `{error: 'unavailable', message}` and only `e.message` on stderr. SKILL.md:38 tells the agent that 3 means "store or connection unavailable ... stop that step; report it in plain words", and headless runs then `run finish --status failed` (SKILL.md:495-497). So a TypeError in a handler (a malformed saved tool response, a null field) is reported to the runner as "memory unavailable", and the stack that would locate it is gone. There is no log file, so the only trace is that message.

## Flow
- ingest-verdicts reads a response shape it does not expect
- a TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined" escapes the handler
- main returns code 3, error unavailable, message only
- agent tells the runner the store is unavailable and stops the step

## Expected impact
Bugs surface as bugs with a location; outages keep code 3. Risk: low; the exit code can stay 3 if the procedure needs it, only `error` and stderr change.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - an internal error is distinguishable from an outage in the CLI output
Before: simulation: TypeError, SQLITE_BUSY and EACCES all print error unavailable, message only
After: simulation: SQLITE_BUSY and EACCES unchanged; TypeError prints error internal with stack on stderr
Method: simulation - walked three exception types through main(); a probe needs a broken handler
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/dowser.mjs:620: const msg = /** @type {Error} */ (e)?.message ?? String(e); | :621: return { code: 3, stdout: `${JSON.stringify({ error: 'unavailable', message: msg }, null, 2)}\n`, stderr: `dowser: ${msg}\n` }; | skill/SKILL.md:38: | 3 | store or connection unavailable, or the command is not built yet | stop that step; report it in plain words; never write the store any other way |
impact_why: Every internal bug is misreported as an outage and loses its stack, slowing diagnosis of field failures

title: A ';' inside a triage reject note splits the entry and refuses the sheet
body:
## Summary
`triage apply --decisions` splits the whole line on `;` and newlines before it reads quotes, so a reject note that contains a semicolon becomes two entries; the tail fails 'starts with a card number' and the whole sheet is refused (nothing moves). The problem is reported as 'line 3' although the person typed one line, and the surviving half keeps a stray opening quote in its note.

## Description
- skill/scripts/lib/triage.mjs:96 `text.split(/[;
]/)` runs before any quote handling; skill/scripts/lib/triage.mjs:84 `unquote` only strips a balanced pair, so the first half's note keeps `"dup of DW-4`.
- skill/scripts/lib/triage.mjs:97 `const line = i + 1;` numbers entries, not lines, and the problem text says `line N`.
- skill/scripts/lib/triage.mjs:167-169 then refuses the batch: `nothing moved; line 3 (same root cause"): starts with a card number (or rest)`.
- skill/SKILL.md:378-381 tells the agent to collect 'the reason codes and notes the runner gave' into one `;`-separated line, so a runner's own prose note is the input.

## Flow
- Runner: '3 reject other, dup of DW-4; same root cause'. Agent writes `1 keep; 3 reject other "dup of DW-4; same root cause"; 4 keep`.
- parseDecisions -> entry 2 note `"dup of DW-4`, problem at 'line 3' `same root cause"`.
- Exit 2, nothing moved; the agent must rephrase the person's note.

## Expected impact
A round-trip with the runner on a natural note, and a confusing 'line 3' for a one-line answer. Fix: split on `;` only outside double quotes (a small tokenizer), and call the counter `entry`.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a quoted note with ';' is kept whole.
Before: probe - parseDecisions returns 3 decisions + 1 problem for 3 intended entries; the note is `"dup of DW-4`.
After: 3 decisions, 0 problems, note `dup of DW-4; same root cause` (quote-aware split walked on the same input and on `2 reject not-worth-it; 5 snooze 2026-12-01` and `rest keep`, which split as today).
Method: probe - ran parseDecisions from a scratch command outside the repo; the fix was simulated on three inputs.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
Probe: parseDecisions('1 keep; 3 reject other "dup of DW-4; same root cause"; 4 keep') -> decisions [{line:1,'1 keep'},{line:2,note:'"dup of DW-4'},{line:4,'4 keep'}], problems [{line:3,text:'same root cause"',problem:'starts with a card number (or rest)'}]. skill/scripts/lib/triage.mjs:96 `text.split(/[;
]/).map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean).forEach((entry, i) => {`.
impact_why: A natural note with a semicolon refuses the runner's whole decision line and mislabels where the problem is.

title: Use the rule.decide and outcome.record answers, not a reflect.data refetch
body:
## Summary
Both Learning writes already return what changed (the rule row; the outcome plus the new candidate list), yet the UI ignores the answer and reruns the whole reflect.data aggregate after every decision.

## Description
Contract: 'rule.decide' -> {rule: RuleRow}, 'outcome.record' -> {outcome, candidates} (forge/src/core/types.mjs:194-195; server forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:449 and :485 `candidates: await candidatesOf(...)`). The UI drops both results (forge/static/app/src/routes/reflect/index.jsx:206, :265) and calls refresh (:207, :266 -> :34 fetchData(true)), i.e. a second invoke of reflect.data, which assembles totals, rejects, notes, pushes, lens_yield, rules, candidates, outcomes and trust (types.mjs ReflectData).

## Flow
- Record an outcome: invoke outcome.record (already computes candidatesOf)
- Then invoke reflect.data: recomputes candidates and every other section
- Per decision: 2 Forge invocations and 2 SQL fans

## Expected impact
Halves Forge invocations per Learning decision and removes the second round-trip latency before the item leaves.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - invocations per decision
Before: 2 invokes (write + reflect.data)
After: 1 invoke; patch d.rules / d.candidates / d.outcomes from the answer, keep a background refresh only for totals if wanted
Method: simulation - counted invoke calls per decision path in reflect/index.jsx against the contract; no Forge metrics reachable read-only
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/types.mjs:194 `'rule.decide': [..., {rule: RuleRow}]` :195 `'outcome.record': [..., {outcome: ..., candidates: OutcomeCandidate[]}]` ; forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:485 `return { outcome: ..., candidates: await candidatesOf(deps, item.project_key) };` ; forge/static/app/src/routes/reflect/index.jsx:265 `await call('outcome.record', payload);` (result discarded) :266 `await onChanged();`

title: validateCandidate is looser than its schema twin in three places
body:
## Summary
model.mjs says it and the JSON Schema must change together, and a test pins enums and caps. Three schema rules have no counterpart in the validator, so a line the store accepts is an invalid `dowser-proposal/2` record.

## Description
1. `provenance.focus` must match `^(goal|area):\S` in the schema; validateCandidate only checks it is a non-empty string (skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:476-478). A candidate line's own focus overrides the run's (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:186).
2. `evidence.quote` has `minLength: 1` in the schema; for non-quoted types the validator accepts `quote: ""` (skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:432).
3. The schema description lists `predicted_why needs predicted_verdict` as validator-only, but `allOf` already expresses the similar `impact -> impact_why`; the schema could carry it too.
The parity tests (skill/scripts/tests/model.test.mjs:106-140) compare enums and caps only, not patterns or minLength.

## Flow
- propose line with provenance.focus 'anything' -> stored, pushed
- a consumer validating with the schema refuses the record

## Expected impact
The validator applies the focus pattern and non-empty quote, the schema gains the predicted_why dependency, and the parity test also compares `pattern`/`minLength` on shared fields.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every record the store accepts validates against its schema
Before: probe: focus 'anything' -> ok true (schema pattern ^(goal|area):\S); ticket quote '' -> ok true (schema minLength 1)
After: both refused with the field named (simulation)
Method: probe - scratch script called the real validateCandidate and read the schema file
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: `focus "anything": true | schema pattern ^(goal|area):\S`; `ticket quote "": true | schema quote minLength 1`; `predicted_why w/o verdict schema allOf? false`; skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:476-478 `for (const k of ['model', 'harness', 'run_id', 'focus']) {\n    if (pv[k] !== undefined && !str(pv[k])) return no(...)`; skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:432 `if (e.quote !== undefined && typeof e.quote !== 'string') return no(...)`
impact_why: Records the store accepts can fail their published schema; consumers of the schema see invalid data
