title: quality-snapshot reads test counts from spec output: TAP on Node 22 writes null
body:
## Summary
tools/quality-snapshot.mjs parses `ℹ tests N` from `npm test` stdout and ignores the exit status; under a reporter other than spec the row records tests: null and tests_fail: null.

## Description
tools/quality-snapshot.mjs:242-244 runs `npm test` piped and matches `ℹ ${k} (\d+)`. The spec reporter prints `ℹ tests 225` (measured on Node 24). On Node 22 (the engines floor, package.json engines `>=22.13.0`) node --test chose TAP when stdout is not a TTY (spec became the non-TTY default in Node 23), whose summary is `# tests 225`, so `num()` returns NaN and JSON.stringify writes null - a value AGENTS.md "Absent values" forbids - and the --append delta at tools/quality-snapshot.mjs:270 compares against null. A crashed suite also reads as NaN rather than fail, because t.status is never consulted.

## Flow
- A campaign on Node 22 runs quality-snapshot --append
- The row stores "tests": null, "tests_fail": null
- The delta line reads tests 225 -> null, and a failing gate is not recorded as fail

## Expected impact
Make the row reporter-independent: run `node --test --test-reporter=spec ...` directly (or parse both `ℹ`/`#` forms) and record tests_status from t.status; omit the keys when unparsed.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the snapshot's gate fields are measured on every supported Node
Before: regex matches only spec output; exit status unused
After: counts parsed on Node 22 and 24; a failing run records fail
Method: simulation - no Node 22 on this machine; probed spec output on Node 24 (`ℹ tests 1`) and walked TAP (`# tests 1`) against the regex
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/quality-snapshot.mjs:242 `const t = spawnSync('npm test', { cwd: ROOT, encoding: 'utf8', shell: true });`; :243 `const num = (k) => Number((t.stdout.match(new RegExp(`ℹ ${k} (\\d+)`)) ?? [])[1] ?? NaN);`; package.json `"node": ">=22.13.0"`; Node 24 probe piped stdout -> `ℹ tests 1`
impact_why: Campaign trend rows silently lose test counts on the supported Node floor; a red suite is not recorded as red.

title: A failed silent refresh leaves a decided rule live, and the retry errors
body:
## Summary
After a successful rule.decide or outcome.record, a failed refresh is swallowed: the decided item stays on screen with its buttons enabled and no message, so the person presses again and gets 'rule ... is accepted, not offered; reload it'.

## Description
useReflect keeps the previous data when a silent fetch fails (forge/static/app/src/routes/reflect/index.jsx:30). RuleOffer/Candidate treat the write as done and clear busy (:207-208, :266-267) with no confirmation. The stale item is indistinguishable from an undecided one. The server refuses a second decision on a decided rule (forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:445 `rule ${id} is ${now?.state ?? 'gone'}, not offered; reload it`), which the UI then shows as an error although the first decision succeeded.

## Flow
- Accept a rule: rule.decide succeeds
- reflect.data refresh fails (storage not ready, network)
- Rule still shows, Accept enabled, no message
- Press Accept again: red error 'rule X is accepted, not offered; reload it'

## Expected impact
The person sees that the decision landed even when the refresh did not; no false error.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a successful write is always acknowledged
Before: silent stale item + misleading error on retry
After: item removed from local state from the write's own answer (see the reflect.data refetch finding), refresh failure at most a quiet 'could not refresh' note
Method: simulation - walked success+refresh-fail, success+refresh-ok, write-fail through useReflect and RuleOffer; the fixture's &fail=reflect.data fails the first load too, so no probe isolates the refresh
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/static/app/src/routes/reflect/index.jsx:30 `(error) => { if (mine === seq.current) setState((prev) => (silent && prev.status === 'ready' ? prev : { status: 'error', error })); },` ; :207 `await onChanged();` :208 `setBusy('');` ; forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:445 `throw new AppError('bad-input', `rule ${id} is ${now?.state ?? 'gone'}, not offered; reload it`);`
impact_why: False error after a successful decision erodes trust in the Learning loop

title: Inbox summaries read the newest push once per inbox
body:
## Summary
inboxSummaries runs one pushes query per visible inbox and a GROUP BY over every proposal of every inbox, on every inbox.list, settings.get and Rovo list call.

## Description
cards.mjs:167 counts proposals of all inboxes (no project filter, so the work grows with inboxes the caller cannot see); cards.mjs:176 queries pushes once per inbox inside the loop. listInbox calls it on every page (cards.mjs:259), so each scroll page costs N+1 extra statements.

## Flow
- site with 20 inboxes
- every inbox page or settings view
- 20 pushes queries plus a full-table GROUP BY

## Expected impact
Summaries cost two statements whatever the inbox count.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - statements per inbox.list
Before: 1 + N statements for N visible inboxes (re-read)
After: one GROUP BY restricted to the visible keys and one pushes read with IN (...) keeping the newest per inbox in memory
Method: simulation - walked N = 1, 5, 20 through inboxSummaries: 2, 6, 21 statements; at 30-60 ms each, 20 inboxes add ~1 s per page

title: Make the page-link backfill resumable instead of restarting from id 0
body:
## Summary
backfillPageLinks walks every proposal in one invocation and marks itself done only at the end, so a run cut by the time limit starts again from id 0 the next day and may never finish on a large site.

## Description
doc-drift.mjs:77 loops from after = 0 over all proposals in pages of 200, with one INSERT per page id (doc-drift.mjs:43 linkPages); the done mark is written only after the loop (doc-drift.mjs:84). It runs after the issue-property backfill inside the same daily migrate invocation (index.js:185-188), with no timeoutSeconds in forge/manifest.yml. No progress cursor is stored, unlike sample.mjs's budgeted, resumable load.

## Flow
- site upgraded with thousands of older proposals
- daily migrate: migrations, property backfill, page backfill
- invocation ends before the loop does
- next day starts again at id 0

## Expected impact
Older items get their byline and banner links within a few days on any site size.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the backfill completes
Before: all-or-nothing loop, progress lost on timeout (re-read)
After: store the last id after each page and stop past a time budget, as loadSample does
Method: simulation - walked 3 sizes: 500 proposals (one run), 5000 with few links (likely one run), 5000 with several page ids each (one INSERT per link, can exceed the budget and repeat daily)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/doc-drift.mjs:77 `for (let after = 0; ;) {`; forge/src/core/doc-drift.mjs:84 `await nextCounter(deps.db, BACKFILL_COUNTER);` (after the loop only)
impact_why: large sites may never get page links for pre-v030 items

title: share --run loses a run's cards once a later run re-sees them
body:
## Summary
`share` picks a run's cards by `last_run_id`, which every later propose line for the same fp overwrites, duplicates included. Sharing an older run after a newer scan touched its cards silently drops them.

## Description
share.mjs promises "Kept = proposed or grown in that run" (skill/scripts/lib/share.mjs:3) but selects `WHERE last_run_id = ?` (skill/scripts/lib/share.mjs:34). propose sets `last_run_id` for any existing fp, even a `duplicate` with no new evidence (skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:255). The run's own evidence rows (`evidence.run_id`) and `first_run_id` hold what the run actually added or created.

## Flow
- run r1 proposes and verifies card A; r1 finished
- run r2 re-proposes A (duplicate)
- share --run r1 -> A missing; cards: 0

## Expected impact
A run's share lists what that run created or grew: `first_run_id = run OR EXISTS evidence with run_id = run`, matching the header.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - an older run's share is stable after later scans
Before: card A leaves r1's share as soon as r2 re-proposes it (walked: r2 created, r2 duplicate, r2 evidence-grew all overwrite last_run_id at proposals.mjs:255)
After: A stays in r1's share in all three cases (first_run_id = r1)
Method: simulation - three cases walked against proposals.mjs:255 and share.mjs:34; not built
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/share.mjs:3 `// Read-only. "Kept" = proposed or grown in that run and still verified, pushed or accepted.`; skill/scripts/lib/share.mjs:34 `SELECT fp FROM proposals WHERE last_run_id = ? AND status IN (...)`; skill/scripts/lib/proposals.mjs:254-255 `const added = addEvidence();\n    db.prepare('UPDATE proposals SET last_run_id = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE fp = ?').run(runId, at, fp);`

title: Eval tools spawn CLAUDE_BIN without a shell: an npm-installed claude.cmd fails
body:
## Summary
dogfood, lens-eval and forge-live-e2e call spawnSync/execFileSync(CLAUDE) directly; on Windows a .cmd launcher cannot run that way, though lens-eval's own npm shim already handles the case.

## Description
tools/dogfood.mjs:303 and tools/lens-eval.mjs:292 `spawnSync(CLAUDE, args, ...)`; tools/forge-live-e2e.mjs:56 `execFileSync(process.env.CLAUDE_BIN ?? 'claude', ...)`. Node refuses .cmd/.bat without shell:true (ENOENT for a bare name, EINVAL for an explicit .cmd since the 2024 CVE fix). The same file knows this: tools/lens-eval.mjs:192-194 quotes and runs a .cmd under a shell for npm. It works on this machine only because claude resolves to C:\Users\kazda\.local\bin\claude.exe (native install); an `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` install is claude.cmd.

## Flow
- A Windows contributor with the npm-installed CLI runs `node tools/lens-eval.mjs --lens doc-drift`
- spawnSync returns error ENOENT; status null
- The tool reports "the scan failed (exit null, spawnSync claude ENOENT)" after building the whole workspace

## Expected impact
Resolve the binary once (where/which, prefer .exe, else run the .cmd with shell and quoted args, as the npm shim does) in the shared harness; the eval tools then run for every Windows install.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - eval tools start on every supported claude install
Before: probe: spawnSync('npm', ['-v']) on this Windows box -> status null, ENOENT (npm is a .cmd)
After: the .cmd path is run through the shell, as tools/lens-eval.mjs:194 already does for npm
Method: simulation - probed the same spawn pattern with npm (a .cmd); claude here is an .exe so the exact failure could not be reproduced without installing
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/lens-eval.mjs:292 `const r = spawnSync(CLAUDE, args, { cwd: w.repo, env, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 45 * 60000, maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 });`; tools/lens-eval.mjs:192 `'// A .cmd needs a shell on Windows; quote the command and every argument for it.',`; probe `spawnSync('npm',['-v'])` -> `null ENOENT`; `where claude` -> C:\Users\kazda\.local\bin\claude.exe
impact_why: Windows contributors on the npm-installed CLI cannot run any eval or dogfood tool.

title: quality-snapshot --append joins an absolute path under the repo root
body:
## Summary
`--append` is resolved with join(ROOT, appendTo), so an absolute path is glued under the repo instead of honoured.

## Description
tools/quality-snapshot.mjs:255 `const file = join(ROOT, appendTo);`. On POSIX, `--append /tmp/q.jsonl` becomes `<repo>/tmp/q.jsonl` - an untracked file written inside the repository; on Windows `C:\x\q.jsonl` becomes `<repo>\C:\x\q.jsonl`, which fails. The sibling tools resolve their paths (tools/dogfood.mjs:184 `resolve(...)`, tools/sample-capture.mjs:55 `resolve(o.out)`).

## Flow
- A campaign passes --append $CAMPAIGN/quality.jsonl (absolute)
- POSIX: the row lands in <repo>/<campaign path>/quality.jsonl, an untracked file in the repo; the campaign file never grows
- Windows: appendFileSync throws ENOENT

## Expected impact
Use resolve(appendTo) (relative paths still resolve from cwd) so the campaign file is the one written.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the row goes where the flag says
Before: path.posix.join('/repo','/tmp/q.jsonl') -> /repo/tmp/q.jsonl
After: resolve('/tmp/q.jsonl') -> /tmp/q.jsonl
Method: simulation - evaluated path.join on both platforms with node -e; three cases walked (relative, POSIX absolute, Windows absolute)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/quality-snapshot.mjs:255 `const file = join(ROOT, appendTo);`; node -e path.posix.join('/repo','/tmp/q.jsonl') -> `/repo/tmp/q.jsonl`
impact_why: Absolute --append writes inside the repo (POSIX) or crashes (Windows).

title: Issue-property backfill failure skips the page-link backfill, mislabelled
body:
## Summary
migrate() runs both backfills in one try, so a failing issue-property backfill skips backfillPageLinks, and a failing page-link backfill is logged as an issue-property failure.

## Description
forge/src/index.js:184-191: backfillIssueProperties then backfillPageLinks inside one try; the catch logs "issue-property backfill failed" (forge/src/index.js:190). These are independent jobs (core/issue-property.mjs vs core/doc-drift.mjs).

- backfillPageLinks never runs that day, so byline/banner links stay missing for pre-v030 items

Before: one failure skips the other and mislabels the log.
After: independent runs, correct labels.

title: A failing user-name batch is swallowed with no log line
body:
## Summary
users.names drops a failed batch silently, so a permanent failure (a revoked read:jira-user scope, a 403) shows raw account ids forever and leaves no trace in the logs.

## Description
forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:221 `} catch { /* omit this batch's names */ }`. Dropping the names is right (forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:210), but the failure is never counted or logged. Other soft failures in the core do log a warn line (forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:327-328).

## Flow
- Jira user/bulk answers 403 after a scope change
- every decider shows as an account id in inbox history
- forge logs show nothing

## Expected impact
Log one warn line per call naming the HTTP status and the batch count, never the ids.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - a degraded nicety becomes visible.
Before: no signal.
After: a warn line with the status.
Method: simulation - walked ok, a transient 5xx and a permanent 403.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:219-221 `const page = await json(await asApp().requestJira(route`/rest/api/3/user/bulk?${q}`), 'Jira user bulk'); ... } catch { /* omit this batch's names */ }`
impact_why: Cheap signal for a silent degradation

title: Page event with an unparseable version date throws instead of being dropped
body:
## Summary
onPageEvent promises "Never throws for a bad event", but a linked page whose event carries a non-ISO version.when throws RangeError, so the edit is not recorded.

## Description
doc-drift.mjs:99 does `new Date(Date.parse(event.content.version.when)).toISOString()` whenever `when` is a string; Date.parse answers NaN for a bad string and toISOString throws RangeError. The doc at doc-drift.mjs:89 says it never throws; the entry point catches and logs (index.js:153-157), so the only trace is a "page event failed" line and the byline loses its page_edited_since_decision flag for that edit.

## Flow
- Confluence sends avi:confluence:updated:page for a linked page
- version.when is a string Date.parse cannot read
- RangeError: Invalid time value
- no page_edits row

## Expected impact
A malformed date falls back to deps.now(), as the absent case already does; the contract in the comment holds.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - documented contract holds
Before: throws RangeError (probe)
After: Number.isNaN(Date.parse(when)) falls back to now(); no throw
Method: probe - scratch script: push a record with doc_impact ["777"], then onPageEvent({content:{id:"777",version:{when:"not a date"}}}) -> "onPageEvent threw RangeError Invalid time value"
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: "onPageEvent threw RangeError Invalid time value"; forge/src/core/doc-drift.mjs:99 `const when = typeof event?.content?.version?.when === 'string' ? new Date(Date.parse(event.content.version.when)).toISOString() : deps.now().toISOString();`; forge/src/core/doc-drift.mjs:89 "Never throws for a bad event."
impact_why: rare malformed events lose one edit stamp; contract mismatch

Before: 2 HelpDialog definitions, 1 rendered

title: Lens direction limit errors name API keys, not the field labels
body:
## Summary
Settings > Lens direction labels its fields 'Focus on' and 'Leave out' and states the limits, but checks nothing client-side; the first a person hears of a limit is the server's message, phrased in API keys.

## Description
The hint promises 'One topic per line, up to 10, each up to 120 characters.' (forge/static/app/src/routes/settings/index.jsx:173) yet the Focus/Leave out textareas have no limit or count (:166, :170) and Save is enabled whenever dirty (:187). The server answers `focus holds 11 items; at most 10` or `each exclude item is one line of at most 120 characters` (forge/src/core/direction.mjs:36, :38), shown verbatim (:149, :192). 'exclude' appears nowhere on screen.

## Flow
- Paste 12 topics into Leave out, press Save
- Red text: 'exclude holds 12 items; at most 10'
- Person has to map 'exclude' to the 'Leave out' box

## Expected impact
Limit errors appear before Save, next to the right field, in the screen's own words.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - error names the field the person sees
Before: post-Save server message with API key names
After: inline count ('12 of 10 topics') per textarea, Save disabled while over; server message mapped to labels as a fallback
Method: simulation - three inputs walked (11 lines, a 130-char line, valid) through LensEditor and direction.mjs lines(); no running UI
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
forge/static/app/src/routes/settings/index.jsx:173 `

One topic per line, up to 10, each up to 120 characters.

` ; :170 `
impact_why: Small, but it is the one place a team steers the scan in its own words

title: Shared-copy check iterates its own SHARED list, not src/shared
body:
## Summary
shared.test.mjs checks only the modules named in sync-shared's SHARED array, so a module copied into src/shared but left off the list is never compared with its source.

## Description
forge/test/shared.test.mjs:13 `for (const name of SHARED)` imports the list from forge/scripts/sync-shared.mjs:18. The ground truth is the directory: today forge/src/shared holds exactly model.mjs and fingerprint.mjs, which equals SHARED, so there is no drift now. The test is derived from the list it should check.

## Flow
- a third pure module is copied into src/shared by hand
- it is not added to SHARED
- it drifts from skill/scripts/lib, and the test stays green

## Expected impact
Assert that readdirSync(forge/src/shared) equals SHARED as a set before the byte check.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the check is derived from the directory.
Before: the coverage is whatever SHARED says.
After: an unlisted file fails.
Method: simulation - listed forge/src/shared today (2 files = SHARED); walked an added unlisted file.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/test/shared.test.mjs:13 `for (const name of SHARED) {`; forge/scripts/sync-shared.mjs:18 `export const SHARED = ['model.mjs', 'fingerprint.mjs'];`; `ls forge/src/shared` -> fingerprint.mjs model.mjs; `node forge/scripts/sync-shared.mjs --check` exit 0
impact_why: Small guard; the drift it prevents is silent

title: dev:local bridge drops the map's project/lens/area deep link and has no banner
body:
## Summary
The two @forge/bridge stand-ins disagree: the fixture bridge carries every inbox deep-link key (ref, project, lens, area) through getContext and router.navigate, the local-server bridge carries only ref, and has no banner surface or view.close.

## Description
bridge.js:320 LINK_KEYS = ['ref','project','lens','area'], used in getContext (:347) and router.navigate (:358). http-bridge.js builds the location with `?ref=` only (:42) and navigate keeps only `ref` (:52-53). A map heat-cell click (routes/map/index.jsx:66-67 -> deeplink.js inboxUrl sets project/lens/area) therefore opens an unfiltered inbox under `npm run dev:local`, the mode that runs against the real store. http-bridge's view has no `close` (vs bridge.js:349) and no 'banner' surface, so the doc-drift Banner (routes/byline/Banner.jsx) cannot be exercised against the local server at all.

## Flow
- npm run dev:local, open #map
- Click a heat cell with 3 open proposals
- Inbox shows every open proposal, not the 3 - looks like an area-filter bug that is not one

## Expected impact
dev:local reproduces Forge's deep links; no false bug reports from the dev path.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - both dev bridges honour the same link contract
Before: http-bridge carries 1 of 4 link keys; no banner/close
After: one shared linkQuery helper used by both bridges; banner surface and view.close in http-bridge
Method: simulation - walked a heat-cell URL through both navigate implementations; dev:local needs the local server running
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/static/app/src/dev/bridge.js:320 `const LINK_KEYS = ['ref', 'project', 'lens', 'area'];` :358 `location.hash = `${route}${linkQuery(u.searchParams).replace(/^\?/, '&')}`;` ; src/dev/http-bridge.js:42 `location: `http://127.0.0.1/jira/apps/local/dowser/${s}${params().has('ref') ? `?ref=${params().get('ref')}` : ''}`` :53 `location.hash = ref ? `${route}&ref=${ref}` : route;`
impact_why: Dev-path only, but it is the path that runs against the real store

title: parseRef reads #L10nProvider as line 10; normalizeAnchor keeps it a symbol
body:
## Summary
The two ref parsers in fingerprint.mjs disagree on symbols that start with `L` and a digit. `normalizeAnchor` only treats a full `L12`, `L12C3`, `L12-L20` fragment as a line; `parseRef` takes any fragment starting `L<digits>` as a line hint.

## Description
`LINE_FRAGMENT` is anchored at both ends (skill/scripts/lib/fingerprint.mjs:29). `parseRef` uses `frag.match(/^L(\d+)/)` with no end anchor (skill/scripts/lib/fingerprint.mjs:100). So `src/i18n.js#L10nProvider` is the anchor `src/i18n.js#L10nProvider` but the evidence ref gets `line: 10`. verify then reports `claimed_line`/`drift` against a line the agent never claimed (skill/scripts/lib/verify.mjs:126-129), and a symbol ref can come out `in-file` instead of a clean in-file match without hint.

## Flow
- evidence ref `src/cache.js#L2Cache` -> parseRef line 2
- quote found on line 140 -> `in-file`, claimed_line 2, drift 138

## Expected impact
One rule: parseRef uses the same anchored `LINE_FRAGMENT` test (and its first number) before reading a line from a fragment.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a symbol ref never produces a phantom line hint
Before: parseRef('src/i18n.js#L10nProvider') -> {path, line: 10}; parseRef('src/cache.js#L2Cache') -> line 2
After: with the anchored test both return {path} only; `#L12` and `#L12-L20` still give 12 (simulation of three cases against the regexes)
Method: probe - scratch script called the real normalizeAnchor and parseRef
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: `src/i18n.js#L10nProvider | anchor: src/i18n.js#L10nProvider | parseRef: {"path":"src/i18n.js","line":10}`; `src/cache.js#L2Cache | anchor: src/cache.js#L2Cache | parseRef: {"path":"src/cache.js","line":2}`; skill/scripts/lib/fingerprint.mjs:29 `const LINE_FRAGMENT = /^L\d+(?:C\d+)?(?:-L?\d+(?:C\d+)?)?$/;`; skill/scripts/lib/fingerprint.mjs:100 `const lf = frag.match(/^L(\d+)/) ?? frag.match(tail);`
impact_why: Misleading drift and claimed_line on symbol refs such as L10n or L2 cache names; verification outcome rarely changes

title: Snooze help promises Enter, Ctrl+Enter does nothing there; reject says fixed 6 s
body:
## Summary
Two help strings state a rule the code does not hold: the shortcut help's snooze line and the Reject dialog's fixed '6 seconds'.

## Description
InboxDialogs.jsx:54 says snooze is 'Enter to confirm' - true only while focus is in a text or date input of the SnoozeStep form (dialogs.jsx:331-334); the Ctrl+Enter rule the help teaches for a and r (InboxDialogs.jsx:52-53) is handled only inside Dialog (ui.jsx:82-87) and the open-dialog listener (useInboxKeys.js:56-73, which returns when no dialog is open), and the snooze step is a form, not a Dialog. RejectDialog says 'You get 6 seconds to undo.' (dialogs.jsx:272) while the window pauses on hover/focus (Toast.jsx:17-18, useCommitWindow.js:74-80) and its length is a parameter (useCommitWindow.js:8, :18), so copy and constant can drift.

## Flow
- Person presses s, tabs to the Snooze button, presses Ctrl+Enter as the help taught for a/r: nothing happens
- Reject copy promises a fixed 6 s although the toast pauses

## Expected impact
Help text a keyboard user can trust; one source for the undo duration.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - help matches behaviour
Before: Ctrl+Enter ignored in the snooze step; '6 seconds' literal
After: snooze step accepts Ctrl+Enter like every dialog (or help says Enter only); reject copy built from COMMIT_MS
Method: simulation - three key sequences walked through useInboxKeys.js, ui.jsx Dialog onKeyDown and the SnoozeStep form; no browser in a read-only scout
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/static/app/src/routes/inbox/InboxDialogs.jsx:54 `['s', 'Snooze, with an optional note and Until date, Enter to confirm ...']` ; :53 `['r', 'Reject ...; 1 to 6 picks the reason, Ctrl+Enter confirms']` ; dialogs.jsx:334 `onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.stopPropagation(); onCancel(); } }}` (no Ctrl+Enter) ; useInboxKeys.js:57 `if (!dialog) return undefined;` ; dialogs.jsx:272 `You get 6 seconds to undo.` ; useCommitWindow.js:8 `export const COMMIT_MS = 6000;`
impact_why: Keyboard-first triage is the inbox's core; help that is wrong costs trust

title: Unit-test triage.mjs parseDecisions: the decision grammar is reached only via the CLI
body:
## Summary
skill/scripts/lib/triage.mjs (196 lines) is the only lib module no test imports; its text parser is exercised only end to end through main().

## Description
Ground truth: of 25 modules in skill/scripts/lib, 24 are imported by a test directly or through the store.mjs facade (proposals.mjs and runs.mjs via store.mjs:23-25). triage.mjs exports triageSheet, parseDecisions and applyDecisions (lib/triage.mjs:67,91,132) and no test imports it; triage-sheet.test.mjs drives it through main() (triage-sheet.test.mjs:5,53), costing 4.3-6.7 s per case. parseDecisions turns a person's free-typed line ("1 keep, 2-3 reject not-worth-it ...") into moves - the input most likely to be malformed - so its edge cases (ranges, duplicates, unknown numbers, trailing text) are cheapest to pin as pure unit tests.

## Flow
- A person types an unusual decision line
- parseDecisions mis-splits it
- Only a slow CLI case could catch it, and only for the lines its four cases happen to type

## Expected impact
A pure test table for parseDecisions (milliseconds) covers the grammar exhaustively and leaves the CLI cases for wiring.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the decision grammar has direct coverage
Before: 0 direct imports of lib/triage.mjs; grammar covered only by CLI cases
After: a table-driven unit test of parseDecisions
Method: simulation - derived the gap from ls skill/scripts/lib vs test imports; walked range, duplicate and unknown-row lines
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: `for m in lib/*.mjs; grep -l "lib/$b.mjs" tests/*.mjs` -> `0 triage` (proposals/runs reached via lib/store.mjs `export * from './proposals.mjs'; export * from './runs.mjs';`); lib/triage.mjs:91 `export function parseDecisions(text) {`
impact_why: The one module parsing free human text has no direct, fast test.

title: Proposal lookups answer before the access check, leaking existence across inboxes
body:
## Summary
acc.proposal runs findProposal first, so a caller who may not open an inbox learns from the error whether a DW ref exists and whether a fingerprint also sits in another inbox.

## Description
access.mjs:82-85 calls findProposal (store.mjs:335) and only then the inbox check. store.mjs:342 answers `no Dowser proposal X` (bad-input) for a missing ref but `forbidden` for one that exists; store.mjs:343 answers "fingerprint X is in more than one inbox" when another, invisible inbox holds the same finding (the same repo scanned by another team). The access module promises the denial "names what would open it, never its content" (access.mjs:26).

## Flow
- caller without access sends proposal.get DW-1..DW-n
- bad-input vs forbidden tells which exist
- an fp lookup reveals that another inbox holds the same finding

## Expected impact
An unopenable inbox reveals nothing, not even existence.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - access denial leaks nothing
Before: two distinguishable answers (re-read)
After: fp lookups filtered to visible inboxes before the ambiguity check; a missing and a forbidden ref answer the same
Method: simulation - walked: ref missing (bad-input), ref in a hidden inbox (forbidden), fp in a hidden and a visible inbox (ambiguity error on the visible one); low stakes: refs are sequential and fps carry no content
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/access.mjs:83 `const p = await findProposal(deps.db, ref);` / :84 `await inbox(p.project_key);`; forge/src/core/store.mjs:342 `if (rows.length === 0) throw new AppError('bad-input', `no Dowser proposal ${r}`);` / :343 `fingerprint ${r} is in more than one inbox; use its DW ref`
impact_why: existence-only leak; refs are sequential and fps carry no content

title: Tool choice can come from a payload-supplied moduleKey
body:
## Summary
mcp() and rovo() accept payload.context.moduleKey as a candidate action key. When the runtime does not set the module key, the payload decides which handler runs, not the action the platform invoked.

## Description
forge/src/index.js:130 and forge/src/index.js:142 pass [runtimeModuleKey(), context?.moduleKey, payload?.context?.moduleKey] to actionName, which returns the first known name (forge/src/core/app.mjs actionName). The action's manifest verb (GET vs CREATE/UPDATE, forge/manifest.yml:42 vs :162) is what Rovo uses to decide whether to ask the person for confirmation. So a GET action whose payload names dowser_verdict_record could record a verdict without that prompt. Whether the platform lets a model put a context key into an action payload is not documented here. Access checks still run on the chosen handler (core/app.mjs TOOLS/ROVO), so this widens the verb, not the data reach.

## Flow
- getAppContext().moduleKey is undefined for the invocation (the fallback exists for that case, index.js:122-123)
- a dowser_inbox_list (GET) call arrives with payload.context.moduleKey = dowser_verdict_record
- the UPDATE handler runs without Rovo's write confirmation

## Expected impact
Drop the payload candidate, or accept it only when it maps to an action with the same manifest verb as the invoked one.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the invoked action alone selects the handler verb.
Before: payload can steer to a write handler.
After: only platform-set keys or shape inference.
Method: simulation - walked runtime key set (no change), runtime key absent with payload key, neither; platform behaviour not probed.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/index.js:142 `const name = actionName('rovo', [runtimeModuleKey(), context?.moduleKey, /** @type {any} */ (payload)?.context?.moduleKey], payload);`; forge/src/core/app.mjs `for (const c of candidates) if (c && known.includes(c)) return c;`
impact_why: Only matters if the runtime key is absent; then a read action can run a write without confirmation
